scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Unlike the traveling Two-Step, Country Swing is a stationary, rotational dance designed for crowded bars, where simple footwork allows for complex, acrobatic 'lifts'.
This is Country Swing. 20th to 21st century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (rP7vsrc5o8g)
Title card: Country Swing · United States · 20th to 21st century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Country Swing's movements originate from mainstream swing dancing, specifically the Jitterbug and East Coast Swing.
It evolved as a country-style adaptation of these forms, tailored for the music and social environments of Western-themed venues.
While it shares a name with the Western Swing music genre, the dance is a specific stylistic branch that prioritizes stationary rotation over the traveling patterns seen in other country dances.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a social, recreational dance used for entertainment and partner interaction.
It serves as a high-energy alternative to the more structured Two-Step, allowing for greater individual expression through acrobatic moves.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a small, stationary space.
The footwork is a simplified 'quick, quick, slow' pattern.
It is a rotational dance where partners move around a central axis rather than traveling across the floor.

The setting is often crowded, which dictates the dance's compact, stationary nature.
Attire is generally casual country-western wear, suitable for the physical demands of lifts and fast rotations.
